{{Short description|American theoretical physicist and historian (1923–2019)}}
'''Laurie Mark Brown''' (April 10, 1923 – October 25, 2019) was an American [[theoretical physicist]] and historian of quantum field theory and elementary particle physics.

==Life and career==
Laurie Mark Brown was born in [[Kings, New York]] on April 10, 1923.<ref>{{cite web |title=Laurie Mark Brown |url=https://www.ancestry.co.uk/discoveryui-content/view/303406975:2238?tid=&pid=&queryId=1c37b1bf-50ed-49fe-8c0c-c8c5b48b38de&_phsrc=Dqh7856&_phstart=successSource |publisher=U.S., World War II Draft Cards Young Men, 1940–1947 |access-date=8 May 2024}}</ref> He studied at [[Cornell University]], where in 1951 he received his Ph.D. under [[Richard Feynman]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Feynman, R. P.|author2=Brown, L. M.|title=Radiative corrections to Compton Scattering|journal=Phys. Rev. |date=15 January 1952|volume=85|issue=2|pages=231–244|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.85.231|bibcode=1952PhRv...85..231B|url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/3611/1/BROpr52.pdf}}</ref> From 1950 he was on the faculty of the physics department of [[Northwestern University]], where he became a tenured professor and eventually retired as professor emeritus. For the academic year 1952–1953 he was at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]]. For the academic years 1958–1959 and 1959–1960 he was a Fulbright Scholar in Italy. In 1966 he was an [[International Energy Agency|IEA]] professor at the University of Vienna. From 1960 to 1970 he served as a consultant for [[Argonne National Laboratory]] and the Laboratory's Accelerator Committee.

Brown was one of the leading science historians for the development of quantum field theory and elementary particle physics, especially in the era after 1945. During the 1990s one focus of his work was the history of modern physics in Japan.

He was the editor for ''Feynman's Thesis: A New Approach to Quantum Physics'' (2005),<ref>{{cite book|author=Feynman, R. P.|editor=Brown, Laurie M.|title=Feynman's Thesis: A New Approach to Quantum Theory|year=2005|publisher=World Scientific|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5kowI7YgFbEC|isbn=978-981-256-366-8|bibcode=2005ftna.book.....B}}; {{cite book|title=pbk.|isbn=978-981-256-380-4|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/feynmansthesisne00feyn_0|publisher=World Scientific|year=2005}}</ref> ''Selected Papers of Richard Feynman, with Commentary'' (2000),<ref>{{cite book|author=Feynman, R. P.|editor=Brown, Laurie M.|title=Selected Papers of Richard Feynman: With Commentary|year=2000|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=978-981-02-4130-8|url=https://archive.org/details/selectedpapersof0000feyn|url-access=registration}}; {{cite book|title=pbk.|isbn=978-981-02-4131-5|last1=Feynman|first1=Richard Phillips|year=2000|publisher=World Scientific |url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/selectedpapersof0000feyn}}</ref> and (with [[John Rigden]] as co-editor) ''Most of the Good Stuff: Memories of Richard Feynman'' (1993).

Brown was one of the founders of the Forum on History of Physics of the [[American Physical Society]] and was the chair of the Forum in 1984 and again in 1989. He was a member of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and a member of the [[History of Science Society]]. In 1961 he was elected a Fellow of the American Physical Society.

Brown died on October 25, 2019, at the age of 96.<ref>{{cite web |title=In Memoriam |url=https://emeriti.northwestern.edu/in-memoriam/ |website=Northwestern University |access-date=2 February 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=In Memoriam: Laurie Brown |url=https://physics.northwestern.edu/people/in-memoriam/laurie-brown.html |website=Weinberg College of Arts & Sciences |access-date=1 February 2025}}</ref>
